svg.text: How the held harmonics are fitted, and how the chain steps in D
The animation loops through five steps. Without animation every step shows at once.

g.text: dashed: degrees 6 and 10, on top of it
order k of the Taylor term
dashed: the first derivative, the tangent
24 terms summed: the prediction at D 229.13
Newton corrects it by about 10⁻³¹ in 3 steps
Below D 73 every harmonic can still be solved. Here is p1 at the centre over one echo period, at six of the 138.
Each wave contains a small harmonic-5 part (drawn 40 times larger). Its cosine coefficient a5 becomes one point against D.
3. Fit a polynomial through the points
A least-squares polynomial of degree 8 in 1/(D−2), times 1/√(D−2), passes within 10⁻¹² of all 138 points.
Past D 73 the polynomial gives the held value. At D 232.6 it sets harmonic 5 of the wave. Fits of degree 6 and 10 differ by 3×10⁻⁹ there.
At a solved D the chain computes the derivatives of the whole solution in D, 24 of them. Their Taylor sum predicts the next D; Newton then corrects it.
